craftinginfo-candela-dipping-text:
Dipping candles
Tallow: the everyday candle, made from what the butcher leaves.

Beeswax candles come from the cooking pot. Tallow candles are dipped, a coat at a time, from melted animal fat.

1. Render the fat. Cook raw fat in a cooking pot into rendered fat, as for an oil lamp.

2. Melt it. Cook rendered fat in a cooking pot again, and it melts into molten tallow, two portions to a lump. Leave the pot on a burning firepit: the fire keeps it molten. Off the fire it soon cools and sets back into rendered fat.

3. Make a dipping rod. A stick and four flax fibers for wicks.

4. Dip. Hold right-click on the firepit with the rod to give its wicks a coat, using one portion of tallow. Let each coat set for a moment before the next, or it will not take. Six coats make finished tapers.

5. Cut them free. A finished rod and a knife in the crafting grid give four tallow candles, and the stick back.
gamemechanicinfo-candela-upkeep-text:
Candles and upkeep

Candles burn down. A beeswax candle lasts about two months of game time, a tallow one about one - unless your server has changed it - and both visibly shorten as they go. Tallow is also a little dimmer, and smokier.

Bunches. Shift right-click to place a candle, or to add one to a bunch, up to nine. Every candle in a bunch burns together. Right-click with a free hand to take one off: a part-burned candle comes back as a stub, which burns for what it has left and places like a candle. Beeswax and tallow do not share a bunch.

Snuffing. Shift right-click a bunch, a lantern or a chandelier with a free hand to put it out and save what is left. Light it again with a lit torch or a firestarter. A lit candle will light a torch, too.

Burned down. A spent candle gutters to a faint glow by default. Your server may have it go dark instead, or not burn down at all.

Lanterns burn one candle at a time - the candle they were crafted with, beeswax or tallow, to begin with. Right-click one with a candle or a stub to put it in; what was left of the old one comes back. Tallow soots the glass and costs a little light. A lantern picked up keeps what is left of its candle.

Chandeliers take beeswax candles or stubs, up to eight, and burn them like a bunch. Right-click with a free hand to take one out, which is how spent candles are cleared.
